title: Von Thomas Next
description: A catering web, proposal, pricing, and operations system with guided menu choices, dependable inventory safeguards, and review-led creative production.
body:
Von Thomas Next is the customer-facing website and operating system behind a real catering business. It helps people understand the offer, choose a suitable menu, receive transparent guidance, and move from an event idea to a useful request. Behind that simple public flow, the product also supports the operational checks needed to turn a confirmed order into dependable preparation.

Catering has many moving parts, but the customer experience should not feel complicated. A customer needs to know what is available, what fits the guest count, and what happens next. The product focuses on clear choices, useful validation, and a proposal flow that does not make people guess.

## What it does

- Lets visitors explore catering offers and send a proposal request online.
- Helps customers compare menus, packages, quantities, and guest-count options.
- Makes pricing easier to trust with stronger checks around portions, package sizes, and menu calculations.
- Supports city and service pages so people can find the right offer for their location and event type.
- Connects paid orders with safer inventory and purchasing workflows instead of relying on manual handoffs.
- Uses review-led workflows for campaign images, short-form video, and print advertising variants.

## Why this project exists

A catering website has to do more than show food. Customers arrive with different needs: a business lunch, a private party, a buffet, or a larger event. They need a quick way to understand what could fit without sending several messages before the first useful answer.

Von Thomas Next turns that first conversation into a guided digital experience. The customer can explore the offer, make informed choices, and send a request with the right context. The same product then helps the team carry that information forward without losing important quantities, inventory context, or pricing safeguards.

## Recent work

The July build concentrated on making menu pricing and fulfillment more dependable. Package calculations now handle fractional sales units more carefully, menu checks validate purchasing assumptions against real package sizes, and existing bread and butter inventory is consumed before suggesting additional purchasing. These changes reduce avoidable over-ordering while keeping the customer-facing menu price grounded in the actual menu configuration.

The operational workflow was also tightened around automated purchasing. Queue, retry, and dry-run safeguards make the workflow easier to review before an action is taken, while inventory and margin audits provide a clearer view of whether a menu can be fulfilled as intended. The goal is not automation for its own sake; it is a safer connection between the offer a customer sees and the work required to deliver it.

Creative production continued alongside the product work. New print-ad concepts and campaign variants were prepared in reviewable formats, while the existing image and short-form video workflow kept creative output tied to real offers rather than generic campaign ideas.

## Value for users

Customers get a clearer route from browsing to a useful catering request. They can understand menu options earlier, see more dependable pricing guidance, and give the team better information from the start.

For the business, the value is continuity. Customer choices, menu calculations, inventory checks, and purchasing preparation stay connected. That reduces repeated manual work and makes it easier to review important decisions before they affect a real order.

## Current direction

The project is moving toward a more dependable end-to-end catering workflow: clear public discovery, guided proposals, trustworthy menu calculations, reviewable creative production, and operational safeguards that support the team after an order is confirmed.
